title: the fight
hook: a monkey tears up Ravana's favorite garden, leaving one tree standing, and then announces exactly whose servant he is
carry: I am the servant of Rama

segments.voice: Yesterday: Hanuman's counsel with himself. The task was done, so he weighed the four ways, and your line, do more, without spoiling it.

At dawn, the birds of the ashoka grove start up in alarm. Trees crash down. Pools are churned to mud. Pavilions come apart. Ravana's most beautiful garden is being taken apart by something huge. The guards wake, and they notice something odd. In the middle of the wreckage, one tree is left untouched: the one Sita sits beneath.
screen: `DAWN, AND THE GROVE COMES DOWN.` → `ONE TREE LEFT STANDING.`

segments.voice: The rakshasi guards turn to Sita. Who is that? What did he say to you? Sita gives a clever answer. How would I know? Rakshasas are the ones who change shape at will. You'd know better than I would. She protects Hanuman and gives them nothing. The guards run to Ravana. Furious, he sends a great company of servants, armed and fierce, to capture the monkey. Hanuman is waiting for them on the gateway arch. He grows huge, slaps his arms, and roars a declaration, which Valmiki gives in full. Victory to Rama, mighty in strength, and to Lakshmana. Victory to King Sugriva, protected by Rama. And then: dāso 'haṃ kosalendrasya. I am the servant of the lord of Kosala, Rama. I am Hanuman, son of the wind. Notice what he says first, in the enemy's capital, at the start of a fight. Not his own strength, though he names it. His loyalty. He says whose servant he is before he says who he is. Then the servants rush him. Hanuman snatches up an iron bar from the gateway and drives them back. It's only the first wave; Ravana will send more, each stronger than the last. Hanuman wanted to see Lanka's strength. Lanka is about to show him.
screen: `ONE TREE, AND SITA, SPARED.` · `HOW WOULD I KNOW?` · `I AM THE SERVANT OF RAMA.` · then, large: `THE FIRST WAVE FALLS.`

segments.voice: Ask yourself, simply and without heaviness: whose am I, what do I serve, love or belong to, a family, a cause, a faith, a craft, a friend? Let one answer come and breathe with it, noticing how it feels to name that before you name anything about yourself.
The fight. Hanuman wrecks Ravana's grove but spares Sita's tree, declares himself Rama's servant from the gateway, and drives back the first wave of guards.
Your line: I am the servant of Rama. Tomorrow, Lanka sends its best. See you then.

howItsDone: Hanuman's declaration of victory to Rama and of himself as Rama's servant is recited by devotees, and some see in it the heart of Hanuman's devotion, dāsya, the love of a servant.

chat.says: When Hanuman shouted at Ravana's guards, what did he say about himself first?
options: That he's the servant of Rama; he named whose he was before who he was.
That he's the strongest warrior alive and no guard could stop him.
That he's Ravana's friend, come to deliver a gift from Sugriva.
chat.meaning: Hanuman's declaration puts loyalty first: victory to Rama, and I am the servant of the lord of Kosala. Only then, I am Hanuman.

ashoka.meaning: a flowering tree; the name means without sorrow

rakshasi.meaning: a female rakshasa; here, Sita's guards

sources.ref: Valmiki Ramayana, Sundara Kanda 41–42 (the grove destroyed; Sita's answer to the guards; the first wave)

notes: Hanuman's declaration (jayaty atibalo rāmo... dāso 'haṃ kosalendrasya...): confirm the sarga (42 in the vulgate, possibly repeated in later sargas) and transliteration.
Sita's answer to the guards (shape-changers would know better): confirm Sundara 42.
Hanuman sparing the tree where Sita sits (the shimshapa / near the chaitya): confirm.
The servants sent first are called kiṅkaras; numbers vary by edition and are omitted.
Trapdoor: dāsya as one of the classic forms of bhakti (e.g., in the Bhagavata's ninefold list); confirm.
